title: Quantitative analyses of products and rates in polyethylene depolymerization and upcycling
author: Lee, Sun, et al.

steps.title: Analyze gaseous products by GC-FID
steps.instruction: Run GC‑FID on the gas stream to obtain a chromatogram, then add propene as an internal standard (propene elutes at 3.2 min) and record a second chromatogram; assign n‑alkanes and iso‑alkanes (C1‑C8) by their retention times.

steps.title: Analyze volatile liquid hydrocarbons by GC-FID
steps.instruction: Dissolve the liquid product in CH₂Cl₂ and inject for GC‑FID; record the chromatogram (solvent peak obscures 2‑4 min region). Evaporate the CH₂Cl₂ solvent, re‑inject, and record a second chromatogram to reveal volatile hydrocarbons in the C7‑C11 range.

steps.title: Record solution‑state 1H NMR spectra
steps.instruction: Prepare an NMR sample of the liquid products and acquire 1H NMR at 20 °C–25 °C (Varian Unity Inova AS600) with an acquisition time of 2.5 s and 64 scans; identify aromatic protons (6.5–9.0 ppm) and benzylic protons (2.0–3.5 ppm).

steps.title: Determine 13C NMR relaxation parameters
steps.instruction: Add Cr(acac)₃ to the NMR sample to a final concentration of 80 mM (22.4 mg in 800 µL CDCl₃) and perform an inversion‑recovery experiment at 25 °C to obtain T₁ (τ/ln2). Use the measured τ ≥ 0.8 s to estimate T₁ ≈ 1.2 s and set the relaxation delay t ≥ 5 × T₁ (t ≥ 6.0 s).

steps.title: Acquire quantitative 13C NMR of heavy liquids
steps.instruction: Prepare the heavy‑liquid sample with the same 80 mM Cr(acac)₃ concentration, then record a quantitative 13C NMR at 25 °C (Bruker Avance NEO 500) using a relaxation delay of ≥ 6.0 s, an acquisition time of 1.5 s, and 4096 accumulated scans; integrate aromatic carbon signals (118–150 ppm) for yield calculations.

steps.title: Perform GC‑MS of heavy liquid fractions
steps.instruction: Inject the heavy‑liquid sample into GC‑MS, acquire the total ion chromatogram, and extract characteristic ion chromatograms for alkylbenzenes, alkylnaphthalenes, alkylphenanthrenes, and alkanes (including naphthenes) to determine average carbon numbers for each class.

steps.title: Conduct size exclusion chromatography of heavy liquids
steps.instruction: Run room‑temperature GPC on the heavy‑liquid sample using chloroform or tetrahydrofuran as eluent; equip the system with RI and/or UV detectors and calibrate with PE or PS standards (e.g., PE 0.120 g, Mw = 3.5 × 10³ g mol⁻¹, Đ = 1.9). For a typical depolymerization (PE 0.120 g, Pt/F‑Al₂O₃ 0.200 g, 1.6 wt % Pt, 0.8 wt % F, 8 h at 280 °C under Ar) compare RI and UV chromatograms to assess molecular‑weight distribution and aromatic content.

steps.title: Run thermogravimetric analysis of solid residue
steps.instruction: Place the solid residue (e.g., PE 0.120 g, Pt/Cl‑Al₂O₃ 0.200 g, 1.5 wt % Pt, 1.4 wt % Cl, after 8 h at 280 °C under Ar) in a TGA instrument, heat in air from 50 °C to 700 °C at 10 °C min⁻¹, and record the mass loss and DTG peaks (PE oxidizes near 300 °C; coke oxidizes at higher temperature).

steps.title: Calculate mass balances and reaction rates
steps.instruction: Using the quantified gas, liquid (volatile C7‑C11 and heavy C>11) and solid yields, compute overall mass balance, selectivities for aromatics versus alkanes, and the average C‑C bond scission rate based on molecular‑weight distribution and product yields.
